summary: Leh Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport is one of the highest commercial airports in the world, situated at approximately 3,256 meters (10,682 feet) above sea level in the Himalayas of Ladakh, India. Named after the revered Buddhist lama Kushok Bakula Rimpochee, it serves as the primary gateway to the remote and culturally rich Ladakh region. The airport presents unique operational challenges due to its high altitude, requiring specialized pilot training and shorter flight windows during the day.
faqs:
Q: Why is Leh Airport considered challenging for pilots?
A: Due to its extreme altitude of over 10,600 feet, surrounded by high Himalayan peaks, pilots require special high-altitude certification and aircraft must be capable of operating in thin air conditions.

Q: When is the best time to fly into Leh?
A: Flights operate most reliably from May to October, as the airport closes during winter months due to snow and harsh weather conditions.

Q: How long does the flight from Delhi to Leh take?
A: The flight typically takes about 1 hour and 20 minutes, though passengers are advised to rest upon arrival to acclimatize to the high altitude.

Q: Are there international flights at Leh Airport?
A: No, the airport primarily handles domestic flights connecting Leh to major Indian cities like Delhi, Mumbai, and Srinagar.
transport_tips: The airport is located about 4 km from Leh town center, and taxis are readily available outside the terminal for the short journey into the city. Pre-paid taxi counters operate inside the arrivals hall, offering fixed rates to popular destinations in and around Leh. Shared taxis and jeeps are also available for budget-conscious travelers heading to nearby villages.
local_tip: Book morning flights whenever possible, as afternoon weather conditions in the Himalayas can deteriorate quickly and lead to delays or diversions to nearby airports like Srinagar.
